forecast-period.text: A weak high pressure system over SA will slowly move over southeastern Australia this week while maintaining a ridge over SA. A trough will pass by the coast mid week before a stronger cold front begins to move into the Bight this weekend.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Morning frost and possible fog on and east of the ranges. Mostly dry, chance of an isolated shower in the far west and Eyre Peninsula in the morning. Maximum temperatures near average, tending below average in the east. Light winds in the east, tending northwest to northeasterly elsewhere. Winds turning southeasterly in the west during the day.
Mostly dry, apart from some showers moving into the far west this evening. Light winds in the south tending northeast to southeasterly in the north.

Morning frost and possible fog on and east of the ranges. Mostly dry, apart from an isolated shower in the morning about the coast. Maximum temperatures near to above average. East to northeasterly winds.

A chance of morning frost on and east of the ranges. Dry in the northeast. Isolated showers developing in the far west during the morning, reaching the eastern districts during the evening. The chance of a thunderstorm in the far west. Maximum temperatures near to above average. Northeast to northwesterly winds, fresh at times over central districts during the day.

text.p: Dry in the northeast. Showers elsewhere, with areas of rain developing across the south during the afternoon. The chance of a thunderstorm about the south, more likely in the evening. Maximum temperatures near average in the south, grading to above average in the north. Northeast to northwesterly winds, tending fresh west to northwesterly during the day.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Saturday: Dry in the northeast. Elsewhere, 2 to 5 mm, increasing to 5 to 10 mm about the agricultural areas, west coast and North West Pastoral district. Isolated higher falls of 10 to 20 mm are possible about the Mount Lofty Ranges and the North West Pastoral district.
